summary: The Hit Squad was a prominent budget re-release label in the UK home-computer market, strongly associated with Ocean's catalogue. Its releases put older full-price, licensed and arcade-derived titles back on sale at lower prices across machines including the Commodore 64 and Amiga.
facts: The Centre for Computing History catalogues numerous The Hit Squad editions explicitly as budget re-releases, including Star Wars on the Commodore 64 and Yie Ar Kung Fu on the Commodore 16/Plus 4.
The museum catalogue includes many Ocean-associated titles under The Hit Squad label, including Rainbow Islands, Batman: The Caped Crusader and WWF WrestleMania.
The museum collection also preserves The Hit Squad releases for the Commodore Amiga alongside its substantial Commodore 64 catalogue.
note: The Hit Squad is treated as a separate re-release label in CCG wherever that credit is explicitly recorded; it does not replace the original publisher credit.

summary: Kixx was U.S. Gold's budget re-release label, returning established computer games to the shelves at lower prices across the late 1980s and 1990s on formats including the Commodore 64 and Amiga.
facts: The Mastertronic Collectors Archive records that U.S. Gold created its own budget label Kixx after previously supplying older full-price titles to third-party budget ranges.
The Centre for Computing History identifies Kixx editions such as Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom as re-releases of earlier U.S. Gold games.
The museum's Kixx catalogue includes Commodore 64 and Amiga reissues across racing, shooting, sports, platform and arcade-derived games.
note: Kixx is additive in CCG: a Kixx re-release credit creates an additional publisher archive association without replacing the game's original publisher.
